name: San Marino
summary: From 2026: securities gains taxed at a flat 10%, domestic dividends 5% final, foreign dividends optionally 3% of the net amount. Residents of more than ten continuous years who are not under a special regime also pay IRAFE, 0.2% a year on listed securities and deposits held abroad above EUR 20,000. Succession tax only reaches San Marino-situs assets (assets abroad are outside it by art. 4 of Law 84/1981); for a spouse and children on San Marino assets it is reported as a fixed EUR 100 per heir (low-confidence source). No other wealth tax. Not in the EU: everyone needs a residence permit; an 'atypical residence' regime (art. 16-ter Law 118/2010) taxes foreign income at 7%, with a EUR 10,000 minimum and EUR 100,000 maximum a year, for up to 15 years, and exempts it from IRAFE.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents pay IGR on worldwide income: progressive 9%-35% (35% above EUR 80,000) on ordinary income, with separate flat rates for capital gains (10%), domestic dividends (5% WHT) and, by option, foreign dividends (3% of net) under the 2026 rules.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident for the majority of the tax period through registered residence, dwelling or centre of vital interests in San Marino; requires a San Marino residence permit for non-citizens.

capital_gains.summary: From tax year 2026 capital gains of individuals on shares, other participations and financial instruments (domestic or foreign) are taxed separately at a flat 10% (Law 166/2013 art. 41 and art. 13 as replaced by Law 141/2025). Real estate gains are taxable only if the property was held 5 years or less; the main home and inherited property are exempt.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Art. 13(1)(b) and 13(2)(b) of Law 166/2013 as replaced by art. 4 of Law 141/2025 (in force from tax period 2026): 'plusvalenze patrimoniali di cui all'articolo 41' taxed separately at 10%. Art. 41(1)(b)-(c) covers disposals of shares, participations and financial instruments; (d) covers sale of a business. Real estate: 0 assumes the property was held more than 5 years (art. 41(1)(a)); a sale within 5 years is taxed at 10%. Via a San Marino intermediary the 10% is withheld as a final tax on 31 December; for foreign-source gains the taxpayer may opt for progressive IGR instead (only useful for small amounts).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Real estate held more than 5 years, main residence, and property received by inheritance are exempt. Losses on securities offset gains of the same year only; no carry-forward (art. 41(6)). LIFO for securities acquired at different times; weighted average cost within an intermediary.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: 2026 reform (Law 141/2025, approved 5 November 2025): the separate-taxation article was rewritten. Pre-2026 tax return forms referred to a 2% substitute tax on financial instruments; how gains were taxed before 2026 was not fully verified. Some secondary sources still claim gains on shares held 12+ months are exempt; that participation exemption applies to companies, not to individuals under art. 41.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains realised within a business (reddito d'impresa) are business income, taxed at 17% (18% for 2026-2030) under art. 13(2)(a) for operatori economici; not researched in detail.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities. Real estate: taxable only if held 5 years or less (donor's holding period added for gifted property).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide income; gains on financial instruments issued by non-residents are taxed at 10% like domestic ones.

dividends.summary: Dividends from San Marino companies: 5% final withholding for individuals (art. 103(6) Law 166/2013). Foreign dividends: by option, separate taxation at 3% of the amount received after foreign withholding ('netto frontiera'); otherwise they enter progressive IGR (9%-35%) with a foreign tax credit.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 5% final WHT. Foreign: 3% on the 'netto frontiera', the foreign income as received net of tax paid in the source state (art. 13(1)(g), 13(2)(e) and 13(3) of Law 166/2013 as replaced by art. 4 of Law 141/2025, read 2026-10-16). There is no credit: the source tax is deducted from the base (foreign_tax_credit 'deduction'). Example: US dividend 100, US WHT 30 (no treaty) -> San Marino tax 3% x 70 = 2.1, total 32.1%.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Collected as a final withholding when received through a San Marino intermediary; the taxpayer may treat it as an advance and opt into progressive taxation.
dividends.important_exceptions: Under the progressive option, foreign tax is credited up to the IGR attributable to that income. Interest on foreign bonds: 10% of net amount by option; interest on foreign bank accounts: 13%.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 5% WHT on dividends paid by San Marino companies to individuals, resident or not; no WHT when the recipient declares it is not acting for an individual (art. 103(6)). Treaties may reduce it.
dividends.treaty_network: Small network (e.g. Italy: 15% portfolio dividends, 0% for 10%/12-month corporate holdings). No income tax treaty with the US, so US dividends suffer 30% US WHT. Network size not verified.
dividends.holding_company_notes: San Marino companies exclude 95% of dividends from non-resident subsidiaries held 12+ months (participation exemption); not verified for 2026.

wealth_tax.summary: IRAFE (imposta per il riequilibrio delle attivita finanziarie estere): 0.2% a year on the market value at 31 December of financial assets held abroad, directly or indirectly, by an individual resident for more than ten continuous years and not under a special regime on foreign income. The first EUR 20,000 is excluded (the Ufficio Tributario computes the tax on the excess). Shares of foreign non-listed companies, shareholder loans, precious metals, foreign banknotes, life and health insurance policies, pension funds and non-financial assets are excluded. No other annual tax on wealth. A new arrival pays nothing for ten years; atypical residents never pay it.
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Not verified whether a recurring municipal property tax exists. Residents must also declare their financial assets and company holdings held abroad each year (DAPEF; reporting).

open_questions: IRAFE in force in 2026? Law 207/2021 art. 4 and the 2024 circular were read; no repeal found in Law 141/2025, but neither the 2024-2026 budget laws nor the delegated decrees were searched line by line.

Art. 4 para. 2 as amended reads 'residente ... da oltre dieci anni continuativi o non assoggettata a regimi speciali' (or). The circular of March 2022 (before the amendment) reads 'da 5 anni continuativi e non assoggettati'; a firm summary (HLB) reads the amendment as ten years. Cumulative ten years is assumed.
Whether the EUR 20,000 exclusion is per taxpayer (spouses holding jointly each get it) was not stated.
Existence and level of any recurring real estate levy.

IRAFE trigger: art. 4(2) Law 207/2021 as amended by art. 17 Law 94/2022 reads 'da oltre dieci anni continuativi o non assoggettata a regimi speciali' (literally 'or'); the Ufficio Tributario circulars read it cumulatively (over 10 years of registered residence and no special regime), which is what is modelled. On the literal reading a new resident outside a special regime would pay it from the start.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: EUR 20,000 of foreign financial assets excluded (art. 4 para. 3 Law 207/2021; circular Prot. 61702/2022: tax on the excess). Tax of EUR 10 or less is not due (art. 4 para. 5-bis, added by art. 17 Law 94/2022). The rate may be changed by delegated decree (art. 4 para. 4).
wealth_tax.eligibility_conditions: Individuals resident in San Marino for more than ten continuous years (art. 17 Law 94/2022, replacing the original five) who are not under a special regime on foreign income such as the atypical residence (art. 4 para. 2 Law 207/2021). The text says 'o' (or) between the two conditions, but the Ufficio Tributario circular reads them cumulatively ('e').
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Assets repatriated to San Marino before the 2021 DAPEF deadline were excluded for 2021 only. Self-assessed in the DAPEF declaration; payment deadline for tax year 2023 was 2 October 2024 (circular of 27 May 2024), so the tax was still being collected in 2024. Not found: any repeal in Law 141/2025 or the 2026 budget (not searched line by line).

components.name: IRAFE on financial assets held abroad
components.notes: 0.2% of the market value at 31 December above EUR 20,000 (art. 4 paras. 3-4 Law 207/2021). Applies only after ten continuous years of residence and never to atypical residents: the model's wealth tax runs from year 1 and so overcharges years 1-10 (see open questions).

inheritance.summary: Succession tax (Law 84/1981) applies only to assets located in San Marino: art. 4 exempts all assets located abroad. For a spouse and descendants it is reported to be a symbolic fixed EUR 100 per heir regardless of value, plus 0.10% stamp duty on the net estate and, for San Marino real estate, 1% transcription and 0.40% cadastral transfer tax. Foreign assets of a resident are outside its scope.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Fixed EUR 100 per heir for spouse and direct-line relatives. Progressive rates apply only to more distant relatives (5%-30% uncles/nephews, 8%-35% great-uncles, 10%-35% others).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Source is a 2015 article by the head of the San Marino Registry Office describing the then-current practice; the 1981 statute's own tariff (in lire, 1%-20% for direct line) was evidently superseded, but the amending act was not located. Inherited real estate passing to foreigners also bears 'imposta di cinquina' (5% for direct line, 10% otherwise) under art. 1 of Law 84/1981; its current status is unverified.
inheritance.gift_tax: Not verified. One Italian advisory page states there is no gift or inheritance tax; registration taxes on gift deeds and the treatment of large gifts of foreign securities were not confirmed.
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for direct-line heirs given the fixed amount.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Situs principle: art. 3 of Law 84/1981 taxes San Marino immovables whatever the deceased's domicile or nationality, and art. 4 expressly exempts movable and immovable assets located outside San Marino and credits not enforceable there. A foreign securities portfolio passing to children is therefore outside the tax (statute read 2026-10-15). Read again 2026-10-16: art. 4 no. 1 'Non sono soggetti a imposta di successione: i beni immobili e mobili posti fuori del territorio della Repubblica'; art. 3 taxes immovables in San Marino whatever the domicile or nationality. The tax file therefore scores the regime as local_assets_only.
inheritance.domicile_rules: No residence-based scope. The heirs' country of residence may tax them.

regimes.name: Residenza atipica (reduced taxation on foreign income)
regimes.description: Residenza atipica soggetta a regime fiscale agevolato (art. 16-ter Law 118/2010, introduced by art. 69 Law 223/2020): a substitute tax replacing IGR on income produced abroad, 7% of the 'netto frontiera' (income net of foreign tax), with a minimum of EUR 10,000 and a maximum of EUR 100,000 for each fiscal year, payable in one instalment with the IGR balance. It is not a fixed lump sum: below the cap the tax is 7% of the foreign income. It ends 15 years after the first tax period (revocable earlier, and lost on any missed or partial payment). Income from San Marino sources and the IRAFE position are outside it: atypical residents are not liable to IRAFE.
regimes.eligibility: Natural persons who have never been tax resident in San Marino (or whose residence was not yet consolidated when the article took effect), who produce income abroad and are not caught by art. 17 paras. 1-2 of the residence law. Application to the Department of Foreign Affairs with a EUR 1,000 fee, a passport copy, a purchase or lease contract for a dwelling, certificates from the previous country of residence, a declaration of nationalities and residences of the last 5 years and proof of sufficient resources; the Congress of State decides within 60 days and its decision cannot be challenged. At most 100 permits a year (not counting extended family members). Spouse and family members listed in art. 16 para. 3-bis can be included on request. Until residence is consolidated (ten years from registration) the holder cannot take public-sector employment, receives no public benefits tied to residence and must carry private or ISS health cover (art. 16-ter paras. 3-14 Law 118/2010 as in Law 223/2020 art. 69).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on foreign securities of a holder of the atypical residence are covered by the 7% substitute tax on the net-of-foreign-tax income, within a EUR 10,000 minimum and EUR 100,000 maximum a year per taxpayer (art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010). Below the cap there is no cut-off: each further euro of foreign gain pays 7%; once the tax has reached EUR 100,000 further foreign gains pay nothing.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010 (art. 69 Law 223/2020, read 2026-10-16): 7% of 'netto frontiera' as defined by art. 13 para. 3 Law 166/2013, minimum EUR 10,000 and maximum EUR 100,000 per tax year. Domestic (San Marino-source) gains stay under the ordinary 10%. The cap and floor are not rates and are not modelled by this rate (see open questions).

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends of an atypical resident are covered by the 7% substitute tax on the net-of-source-tax amount, inside the EUR 10,000 to EUR 100,000 annual band (art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010).
dividends.rate_basis: 7% of the foreign dividend as received net of source tax (art. 16-ter para. 2 Law 118/2010 with art. 13 para. 3 Law 166/2013); no credit, the source tax comes off the base (deduction). Minimum EUR 10,000 and maximum EUR 100,000 per taxpayer and year are not modelled by the rate. Whether an atypical resident can instead elect the ordinary 3% foreign-dividend option was not verified; the substitute tax is by law the tax on foreign income.

cost_of_living.city: San Marino (Città di San Marino / Borgo Maggiore)

intl_school_annual_fee.description: San Marino has no international school; this is the International School of Bologna (IB Continuum school, about 135 km by road from San Marino, the nearest verified IB school a San Marino family would realistically use), 2026–27 annual tuition for Grades 11–12: EUR 21,870, plus an annual registration fee of EUR 1,000 (Grades 11–12) and a one-off EUR 1,500 admission fee. IB exam fees, books and insurance are included; lunch is extra. Daily commuting from San Marino is not realistic, so in practice this implies boarding/relocation or an Italian or Sammarinese private school instead.

source.title: ISB Tuition Fees 2026-2027 (fee schedule embedded in the Tuition Fees page)

cost_of_living.notes: School fee is for the International School of Bologna (Italy), because San Marino has no international school. Rent is the median of two 3-bedroom villas on Mioaffitto.it (2026-10-15); no 4-5 bedroom long-let was listed, Immobiliare.it, Idealista and Casa.it block automated access, and the .sm agency domains tried (immobiliare.sm, smimmobiliare.sm) do not resolve.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median of the two largest homes for long-term rent in the Republic of San Marino on Mioaffitto.it (an Italian portal aggregating agency ads) on 2026-10-15: a furnished 220 m² detached villa in Torraccia (Domagnano) with 3 double bedrooms, a tavern level and garden (EUR 2,300/month) and a furnished 260 m² detached villa in Casole (Città di San Marino) with 3 bedrooms on a 1,000 m² plot (EUR 2,000/month; its text also says 'in vendita', so it may be offered for sale too). The page listed 11 San Marino rentals (Domagnano, Borgo Maggiore, Città, Dogana); none had 4–5 bedrooms, and the other large units were flats of 110–168 m² at EUR 1,000–1,500. Very thin sample; 3-bedroom villas are used as the closest available proxy for a prime family home. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.
